rejected.title: Evidence, opinion and anecdote
card: Evidence
Scientific evidence comes from observations or measurements made under controlled conditions. Others can repeat the work and check the result.
Opinion
a personal view or belief. It may be well informed, but it has not been tested, so it cannot settle a scientific question.
Anecdote
a story about one person's experience. It was not collected under controlled conditions and nobody can repeat it, so it cannot settle a scientific question.
Opinion and anecdote can suggest an idea worth testing. Only tested, repeatable evidence can show whether the idea is supported.
rejected.remember: Evidence can be tested and repeated. Opinion and anecdote cannot, so they cannot settle a scientific question.

a.q: Why can an anecdote not settle a scientific question?
opts: It was not tested in a controlled way and cannot be repeated
It comes from a person who is not a trained scientist
It is always false when it describes a chemical reaction
It has been tested many times but gave unclear results
a.why: An anecdote describes one experience that others cannot repeat or check. It may be true, but that alone does not make it evidence. Who tells it does not matter: the problem is that it was never tested.
a.clue: Think about whether anyone could repeat and check the story.

b.q: Liam says his gran's tea stain remover works, because it cleaned his shirt once. Which step would turn this claim into scientific evidence?
opts: Test it on many identical stains and compare with a control
Ask more family members whether they think it works
Ask a chemistry teacher for their opinion on the claim
Wait to see if the remover cleans his shirt again
b.why: Evidence needs controlled tests that others can repeat, such as many identical stains compared with a control. The other options add more opinions or one more story. A teacher's view is still an opinion, and one repeat on a single shirt is still an anecdote.
b.clue: Does adding more views or one more story make the claim tested?
